english.html: A prodigious History of a supposed
husband, which befell in our time:
enriched with one hundred and eleven fine
By Master Jean de Coras, Counsellor in the
Court, and reporting judge of the case.
Pronounced at the general sessions, the twelfth of
For Galliot du Pré, at the first pillar
of the great hall of the Palace.

french.text: mary, aduenüe de noſtre temps: en-
Par M. Iean de Coras, Conſeiller en la
Prononcé és Arreſtz generaux, le xij.
Pour Galliot du Pré, au premier pillier
de la grand' ſalle du Palais.

uncertain.note: manuscript shelf/accession number written in brown ink in a later cursive hand in the blank margin above the woodcut border; NOT printed and so not entered as a block. Best reading 'N.º 277'; the last figure carries a curl and a dot above it, so it could be read as '2771', '2772' or '277.' — the digits are looped cursive and the '2' could also be a '9'.

set in the largest capitals on the page with light letterspacing (gap roughly a quarter of a letter width), far narrower than the wide spacing of A R R E S T, A  P A R I S and M.  D.  L X X I I.; treated as an ordinary capital word, spaced_caps not set. Reconciler may wish to make this uniform across blocks[1]-[3].
moderately letterspaced capitals, between MEMORABLE and A R R E S T in width; spaced_caps not set, on the same judgement as blocks[1]

the most strongly letterspaced of the three smaller capital lines (gap near half a letter width); borderline for §3 spaced capitals, but transcribed as an ordinary capital word for consistency with blocks[1]-[2]

a small faint caret/grave-shaped mark stands over the 'o' of 'prodigieuſe'; it is much lighter than the type and the word needs no nasal bar, so it is read as an ink speck or offset and transcribed as a plain o

uncertain.text: mary, aduenüe de noſtre temps : en-
uncertain.note: a faint tilde/caret-shaped mark is printed over the 'm'/'a' of 'mary'; 'mary' (= mari) needs no abbreviation and the mark is lighter than the surrounding type, so it is taken as a speck or offset. 'aduenüe' carries a clear diaeresis on the u. A space is printed before the colon in 'temps :' and has been kept.
the word-break sign after 'annota' is printed as a short double stroke, the lower stroke dropping below the line so that it can be mistaken for a comma; transcribed as a single '-' per §1

the four figures are set with visible spaces between them (1 5 6 0); normalized to '1560' per §1 since they are numerals, not spaced capitals. The third figure is a 6 (1560 is the date the arrêt was pronounced, the book being of 1572).

uncertain.text: A  P A R I S,
uncertain.note: the comma is set clear of the final S with a space before it; attached to the S here per the whitespace rule in §1

uncertain.text: Pour Galliot du Pré, au premier pillier
uncertain.note: the final 'r' of 'pillier' is faint and partly broken away at the right edge of the printed panel; read as 'pillier' from sense

uncertain.text: M.  D.  L X X I I.
uncertain.note: widely letterspaced; read as M. D. LXXII. = 1572. The five numerals after D. are L X X I I with no sign of a further stroke.

the title panel is crossed throughout by heavy show-through/offset from the printed text on the other side of the leaf (the privilege), which produces ghost lines of type behind and between the title lines; none of it belongs to this page and none has been transcribed
the title page has no running head, no printed folio (the manifest gives folio null), no signature and no catchword; the space below the border is blank

readings.reason: all 19 lines identical in both reads; B keeps the border and device in the ornaments list rather than as ornament blocks, which is the ruling for the title page (ornament blocks are for ornaments inside the text column)
